suppressions.reason: Windows Installer 'Note: 2205/2228/2262/2727' lines are internal queries for optional database tables. They appear in almost every healthy MSI log and are not errors.

suppressions.regex: translated to success due to continue marking
suppressions.reason: A WiX custom action marked 'continue' reported an error that the installer deliberately ignored.
WiX helper clean-up steps (stopping a process that is not running, removing a folder that is not there). They only matter if the same action later fails fatally.
The installer skipped an action because its condition was false. That is normal and includes error-sounding names such as NewerVersionError.
Windows Installer routinely checks each package against software restriction policy. This line is the check running, not a block.
Application-compatibility probe that fails to initialise on most installs. Harmless.
Windows Installer property dump. Values such as ErrorDialog=SetupError are just configuration.

suppressions.regex: getting the main module name for process
suppressions.reason: ScriptRunner enumerating running processes cannot read protected system processes (csrss, System). Expected for SYSTEM and harmless.
Configuration values echoed at start-up. Settings, not events.

suppressions.regex: \[Flighting\d?\] (?:Key: [^,]+, value not found\. Falling back to default value|CheckEnabledFlights:)
suppressions.reason: Intune feature-flag lookups. IME logs a fallback to the default for every flag the service has not set; it is not an error.

suppressions.regex: Not registering the new Channel URI as the previous channel is yet to expire|co-mgt features is not available|Found native machine from WoW\d+ process|Failed to parse (?:appResultCreatedTimeUTC|downloadStartTimeUTC)|EspHelper\]\[CheckEspPhase\] Not found instance|The EspPhase: NotInEsp
suppressions.reason: Status messages that Intune Management Extension logs at warning or error level during normal operation (no co-management, not in the Enrollment Status Page, and so on).

suppressions.regex: (?:application|policy) poller (?:starts|stopped)|\[HS\] Runner.*(?:Runner starts|Refresh session info|Processing user session|Completed user session|run State = RunLater|queued time .* is expired)|\[Win32App\] Refresh session info
suppressions.reason: Scheduler heartbeat lines from the app and remediation script pollers.

suppressions.regex: LogonUser failed with error code : \d+|AAD User check using device check in app is failed, now fallback to the Graph audience|Failed to get proxy info for session id \d+
suppressions.reason: Intune probing a user session it cannot log on to (for example with nobody signed in) before falling back to device-level checks. Common and not a failure by itself.

suppressions.regex: \[HS\] (?:exit code of the script is|Returned exitcode from child process is) \d+|Powershell execution is done, exitCode = \d+|SideCarScript(?:Detection|Requirement)Manager Powershell ExitCode: \d+
suppressions.reason: Exit codes from detection and remediation scripts. For these, a non-zero code usually means 'not compliant' or 'not detected', which is a result, not a failure.
DCOM permission warnings (event 10016). Windows logs these constantly and they are almost never the cause of anything.
Text reporting that there were no errors.
